case.title: Cart total is ₹0.01 lower than it should be for some products
case.summary: The cart was under-charging GST by ₹0.01 for products with non-whole-rupee prices (e.g. Cast Iron Tawa at ₹1,049.25). The culprit commit 98e2fcea changed computeTotals() to compute tax via roundMoney(sumBy(lines, l => l.lineTotal * GST_RATE)) — floating-point multiplication per line before rounding — instead of calling the existing calculateGst() helper that converts to integer paise first. The fix restores the correct call: tax = calculateGst(subtotal), with a matching import update. The repro test (tests/bugproof/case_20260926_b86b.test.ts) went from red (₹188.86) to green (₹188.87), and all 120 tests pass.

plainSummary.text: The cart subtotal was being calculated incorrectly for products with non-whole-rupee prices, causing GST to be slightly off by ₹0.01. This happened because the new code multiplied the line totals by the GST rate using decimal floating-point numbers before rounding, which introduced a tiny error. The fix restores the previous correct method of converting to integer paise first and uses a dedicated helper function to calculate GST accurately.

data.summary: This commit replaced calculateGst(subtotal) with roundMoney(sumBy(lines, l => l.lineTotal * GST_RATE)), dropping the integer-paise rounding path and introducing the one-paisa rounding error for non-whole-rupee prices.

callers: calculateGst() in src/tax/gst.ts (correct but not called from totals)
roundMoney() in src/currency/money.ts (used by totals, coarser than paise-first)
data.notes: Bug is in computeTotals() which uses floating-point GST_RATE multiplication then roundMoney() instead of the already-correct calculateGst(). Only non-whole-rupee prices are affected (whole-rupee amounts avoid the half-up edge case).

data.expected: GST ₹188.87 (18% of ₹1,049.25, rounded half-up) and total ₹1,238.12
data.actual: GST ₹188.86 and total ₹1,238.11 — one paisa short; customers under-charged
stepsToReproduce: Add Cast Iron Tawa (₹1,049.25, qty 1) to empty cart
Check cart summary GST and total lines

reasons: Fix is correct: calculateGst() in src/tax/gst.ts multiplies integer paise by the rate percent then divides by 100 and rounds, eliminating the floating-point precision loss that caused the one-paisa shortfall.
Fix is minimal: only the tax computation line and its import changed; no unrelated behaviour was altered in src/cart/totals.ts.

Repro test is specific: tests/bugproof/case_20260926_b86b.test.ts asserts both totals.tax === 188.87 and totals.total === 1238.12 using the exact problematic unit price (₹1,049.25), directly encoding the reported expected behaviour rather than gaming the assertion.
